Implementation Plan

Planning ref
- HEAD: `04ec3d1211c9ac53fc365c01c8c736a8d3563c84`

Clarification mapping
- No Q1/Q2 clarification set was issued.
- The `/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]` comment is only the continuation marker, so the issue body is the authoritative scope.

Automation / wiring
- Change type: extend existing workflow + existing reviewer launcher; no new scheduler entry, no new supervisor, no DB work.
- Existing entry point to wire through: `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` on its current PR / `workflow_dispatch` triggers.
- Scope constraint from the issue: keep the Phase I tier logic inside the listed files; do not add a standalone resolver script in this phase.

Representative pattern inspected
- Reviewer-side pattern: `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` existing `classify_reviewer_risk_tier` + `resolve_active_reviewer_models`.
- Workflow-side pattern: `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` existing `Evaluate review gate` and `Run reviewer models` flow.
- Test pattern: `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py` existing risk-tier harness.

Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`
  - Add additive `REVIEW_TIER_*` env defaults in both the top-level env block and the `codex-agent` job env block.
  - Reuse the existing `[force-review]` / `force-review` check in `Evaluate review gate` to export a downstream “force full tier” signal without changing the current skip decision logic.
  - Ensure the launcher’s resolved tier can turn `REVIEW_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED=0` for `lite` runs only.
- `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`
  - Inline a new Phase I review-tier resolver (`lite` / `standard` / `full`) next to the existing risk-tier helpers.
  - Reuse current diff/changed-file artifacts and live reviewer-model normalization.
  - Export the resolved tier/reason for downstream workflow steps and apply the tier-specific reviewer subset when the new flag is enabled.
- `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py`
  - Add a focused resolver harness/test covering `lite`, `standard`, `full`, and force-full override behavior.
  - Extend workflow env wiring assertions for the new `REVIEW_TIER_*` vars.
- `README.md`
  - Document the new Phase I flags/thresholds and how they interact with `AUTOFIX_SKIP_*`, `[force-review]`, and consolidator skipping.
- `agents.md`
  - Mirror the README contract updates in the review-pipeline facts + env table.

Functions / modules to implement
- In `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh`
  - Add a new helper block that resolves `REVIEW_TIER` and `REVIEW_TIER_REASON`.
  - Gate the new path behind `REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED`; when false, preserve current behavior.
  - Use the repo-local Phase I rules:
    - `lite`: doc-only path set matching the existing `AUTOFIX_SKIP_DOC_ONLY` glob semantics, plus LOC <= `REVIEW_TIER_LITE_MAX_LOC` (default 50).
    - `standard`: changes confined to one allowed top-level directory (`scripts/`, `prompts/`, `.github/workflows/`, or `tests/`) and LOC <= `REVIEW_TIER_STANDARD_MAX_LOC` (default 200).
    - `full`: everything else, all fail-open cases, and any forced-full override.
  - Route reviewer fan-out by resolved tier when enabled:
    - `lite`: single configured reviewer slug.
    - `standard`: configured reviewer subset list.
    - `full`: full live roster.
  - Reuse existing live-roster validation/fallback behavior so unknown configured slugs fail open to the full set.
  - Export `REVIEW_TIER`, `REVIEW_TIER_REASON`, and (for `lite`) `REVIEW_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED=0` via `GITHUB_ENV`; optionally also persist a small runtime file analogous to `reviewer_risk_tier.txt`.
- In `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`
  - Add the new config vars:
    - `REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED` (default `false`)
    - `REVIEW_TIER_LITE_MAX_LOC`
    - `REVIEW_TIER_LITE_REVIEWER_SLUG`
    - `REVIEW_TIER_STANDARD_MAX_LOC`
    - `REVIEW_TIER_STANDARD_REVIEWER_SLUGS`
  - Keep deterministic skip authoritative: if `AUTOFIX_SKIP_*` already short-circuits, this new resolver never changes that path.
  - Preserve `[force-review]` / `force-review` semantics by surfacing a downstream “force full” signal from the existing gate.
- No new `scripts/review_tier_resolver.sh` in Phase I.
- No `scripts/review_consolidate.sh` change is required if the workflow/launcher reuses its existing `REVIEW_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED=0` early-exit gate.

Data structures / runtime artifacts affected
- New additive env/config surface:
  - `REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED`
  - `REVIEW_TIER_LITE_MAX_LOC`
  - `REVIEW_TIER_LITE_REVIEWER_SLUG`
  - `REVIEW_TIER_STANDARD_MAX_LOC`
  - `REVIEW_TIER_STANDARD_REVIEWER_SLUGS`
- New per-run resolved state:
  - `REVIEW_TIER`
  - `REVIEW_TIER_REASON`
  - force-full signal from the workflow gate
- Existing `REVIEW_CONSOLIDATOR_ENABLED` is reused as the runtime skip switch for `lite`.
- Existing reviewer risk-tier files/envs stay intact for backward compatibility.

API / interface changes
- Additive only; no renames.
- The new resolver is default-off during acceptance (`REVIEW_TIER_RESOLVER_ENABLED=false`).
- Existing `REVIEWER_RISK_TIER_*`, `REVIEWER_TIER_TRIVIAL_MODELS`, and `REVIEWER_TIER_LITE_MODELS` contracts should remain documented and untouched while the new flag is off.
- No GitHub API contract change is needed.

Risks / edge cases
- Do not let the new tier resolver alter the existing `AUTOFIX_SKIP_*` fast paths or the deterministic-skip merge tail.
- `[force-review]` / `force-review` must force `full` even when the diff would otherwise be `lite` or `standard`.
- Because `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` already has legacy `trivial | lite | full` risk-tier logic, the new `lite | standard | full` review-tier resolver must be additive, not a rename.
- Fail-open cases (missing diff, unreadable changed-files list, invalid configured reviewer slug) should resolve to `full`, with consolidator still enabled.
- Use raw PR paths for shape checks/override safety; avoid accidentally down-tiering a broad PR just because reviewer-visible filtering removed low-signal files.
- Keep Phase I scoped: no new stable log-prefix contract and no new support-script staging churn unless strictly required.

Testing considerations
- Extend `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py` with a focused resolver harness patterned after the current risk-tier harness.
- Cover at least:
  - `lite` resolution
  - `standard` resolution
  - `full` resolution
  - force-full override
  - invalid/missing configured reviewer slug(s) failing open to full
  - workflow env wiring for the new vars/defaults
- Prefer inline patch text in the test over adding new fixture files if that keeps the touched-file set smaller.
- Re-run the existing risk-tier assertions in the same test file to ensure the legacy path still behaves the same when the new flag is off.

Conflicts noted
- The current codebase already has documented `trivial | lite | full` reviewer risk-tier routing; the requested `lite | standard | full` review tier is a second, additive routing layer.
- `docs/plans/gstack-learnings-plan.md` describes a broader Phase I shape with a new `scripts/review_tier_resolver.sh`, but this issue explicitly narrows scope to the listed files, so the resolver should be inlined into `scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh` instead.
- That same plan doc cites `x-ai/grok-4.1-fast` in the standard-tier subset, but the live workflow roster on this ref uses `x-ai/grok-4.20`; new default subset values must align to the live roster, not the stale slug.

Assumptions
- Phase I should reuse the repo-local naming/threshold contract from `docs/plans/gstack-learnings-plan.md`, but implement it inline to respect issue scope.
- The only behavior change required in this phase beyond reviewer routing is “skip consolidator on `lite`”; parser/editor/consolidator helper internals stay unchanged.
- Acceptance rollout is protected by the default-off flag, so preserving exact current behavior when the flag is false is mandatory.

Missing-context notes
- The issue body does not restate the exact default reviewer subset slugs, so the plan derives them from the repo-local Phase I plan plus the live `REVIEWER_MODELS` roster.
- The issue does not request summary/report UI changes, so this plan keeps observability limited to launcher/workflow-exported tier state.
